programs.statusNote: New NOFO being released by DCEO. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: $250K–$1M. Seed and predevelopment funding for Equity Eligible Contractors and equity-building projects.

programs.name: Community Solar Energy Sovereignty Grant (CSES)
programs.statusNote: New NOFO being released by DCEO. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Up to $8.5M/yr. Predevelopment and development for community-owned solar. Municipalities and community organizations.

programs.name: Clean Energy Contractor Incubator
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Business development, bonding and insurance support for small and equity eligible contractors.

programs.name: Clean Energy Primes Accelerator
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: Capital access and prime-contractor readiness for established equity eligible firms.

programs.name: Clean Jobs Workforce Hubs
programs.statusNote: Clean Jobs Workforce Network Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Regional training and placement. Note: CEJA workforce training funding opportunities are closed; DCEO says check back fall 2026.

programs.name: Climate Works Pre-Apprenticeship
programs.statusNote: Climate Works Pre-apprenticeship Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Pre-apprenticeship pipeline into building trades for clean energy work.

programs.name: Energy Transition Navigators
programs.statusNote: Energy Transition Navigator Program NOFO open. Applications due October 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Community outreach staff who connect residents and businesses to CEJA programs.

programs.name: Energy Transition Community Grants
programs.statusNote: NOFO coming soon. Watch DCEO grant opportunities.
programs.detail: For communities affected by plant or mine closure. Awards sized to property tax and job losses.

programs.name: Illinois Home Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.statusNote: Delivered year-round through local agencies. Federal WAP funded at $329M for FY26. Apply through your local community action agency.
programs.detail: Income-qualified weatherization and efficiency measures delivered through local agencies.

programs.name: CEJA Program Map
programs.detail: Live map of workforce hubs, contractor programs, EJ and R3 community layers.

programs.name: Illinois Shines (Adjustable Block)
programs.detail: Illinois Shines is a state-administered solar program that provides incentives for the development of qualified solar projects, including on-site (distributed generation) and community solar through the purchase of Renewable Energy Credits, or RECs by Illinois utilities. RECs represent the environmental value of energy generated by renewable sources, including solar. Click the link below to learn more

audience.label: Illinois Shines — Exploring Solar
audience.detail: Depending on your specific circumstances, a Distributed Generation project installed on your home or property might make the most sense, or a subscription to a local Community Solar project could be preferable.

audience.label: Illinois Shines — Become an AV or Designee
audience.detail: A state-administered solar program that provides incentives for the development of qualified solar projects inlcuding on-site (distributed generation) and community solar through the purchase of Renewable Energy Credits by Illinois utilities. To learn more about how to get involved, follow the link below.

audience.label: Illinois Shines — Solar for Schools
audience.detail: Illinois Shines provides resources designed for public schools to discuss, plan, and implement solar projects. Check out these resources, and watch a recorded presentation (or read the presentation slides) covering the details of the Public Schools category. You can also begin by requesting a tailored workshop for your school or to talk to an Illinois Shines Public Schools Strategist.

statusByAudience.statusNote: The Illinois Shines program is open from June through May of each year. Available capacity can be monitored through the [Block Capacity Dashboard](https://illinoisshines.com/project-status-and-capacity-dashboard/).

programs.name: Illinois Solar for All
programs.statusNote: The state-funded program continues. The separate federal Solar for All award that would have expanded it was terminated in August 2025; courts vacated that termination in September 2026 but money has not resumed. Treat any federal expansion as unavailable.
programs.detail: Illinois Solar for All is a state program that makes solar energy more affordable for income-eligible residents and the organizations that serve them. Participants are served through Approved Vendors which are qualified and vetted solar companies. In most cases, there are no-upfront-cost solar for income-qualified households, non-profits and public facilities in or adjacent to environmental justice and income-eligible communities. Illinois Solar for all serves eligible participants through three sub-programs: Residential Solar, Non-Profit & Public Facilities, and Community Solar.

audience.label: Illinois Solar for All — Vendor Home
Illinois Solar for All — Non-Profit & Public Facilities
audience.detail: Non-profit leaders and public administrators can lower electricity costs for their organizations by installing solar panels directly on their property through Illinois Solar for All. Additionally, a single non-profit or public facility can also save money on electric bills by serving as a Community Solar “anchor subscriber.”

statusByAudience.statusNote: The Illinois Solar for All program calendar is updated each PY and includes project submission deadlines: https://www.illinoissfa.com/vendors/calendar/

programs.name: CRGA Energy Storage Procurement
programs.detail: 20-year Indexed Storage Credit contracts for standalone, utility-scale storage. Initial procurement conducted August 2026 targeting 1,038 MW, split between MISO Zone 4 and the PJM ComEd area; those projects must reach commercial operation by Dec 31, 2029. Procurements continue until 3,000 MW is committed by Dec 31, 2030. Bidders must meet the Minimum Equity Standard and Prevailing Wage Act and execute a Project Labor Agreement.

programs.name: CRGA Implementation Hub
programs.detail: Public Act 104-0458, signed Jan 8, 2026, effective June 1, 2026. The IPA's implementation hub, updated as work progresses: storage procurement, Storage for All evaluation, virtual power plants, expanded efficiency, thermal energy, and the state's first Integrated Resource Plan, due to the ICC by Nov 15, 2026.

programs.name: C-PACE Financing
programs.detail: Long-term financing repaid through a voluntary property assessment. Up to 25% of property value. Existing buildings and new construction. Not available to government-owned property, which includes public community college and university campuses.

programs.name: SSBCI Loan Participation
programs.detail: Participation loans of $25K–$2M. IFA purchases up to 50% of a loan at 2%, or 1% for socially and economically disadvantaged and very small businesses. Must apply through an enrolled lender, not directly.

programs.name: Climate Bank Financing Directory
programs.detail: All Climate Bank programs sorted by who you are: residents, developers and contractors, local governments and nonprofits, municipal and cooperative utilities.

programs.name: DG / EE Measures / EV Installer Certification
programs.statusNote: Rolling. EE Measures recertification due June 1 each year.
programs.detail: Required before a contractor can install for others or touch utility incentive money. Rolling applications. EE Measures recertification due June 1 annually.

programs.name: Equitable Energy Upgrade Program
programs.statusNote: Still in ICC rulemaking (Docket 25-0863) as of October 8, 2026. No tariff in effect.
programs.detail: Tariffed on-bill program. Still in rulemaking (Docket 25-0863). Delivered through utility tariffs, not directly by ICC. Do not build a capital stack on it yet.

programs.name: ComEd Energy Efficiency (Business & Residential)
programs.detail: Prescriptive and custom incentives, free assessments, instant discounts, small business direct install. Part of the ICC-approved 2026-2029 plan. ComEd serves northern Illinois only: roughly Iroquois County and I-80 north to Wisconsin, Iowa border to Indiana border. If your electric bill does not say ComEd, this is not your program.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Standard and custom business incentives, retro-commissioning, income-qualified programs. Ameren Illinois serves central and southern Illinois, about 1.2 million electric and 800,000 gas customers across 40,000 square miles. Not available in ComEd territory.

programs.name: Nicor Gas Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Gas efficiency rebates, public sector custom incentives and on-bill financing. CRGA lets Nicor, Peoples and North Shore pursue increased energy reduction goals. Nicor serves most of the northern third of Illinois but NOT the city of Chicago, which is Peoples Gas.

programs.name: Peoples Gas / North Shore Gas Energy Efficiency
programs.detail: Gas efficiency rebates and direct-install programs. Peoples Gas serves the city of Chicago; North Shore Gas serves the northern suburbs in Cook and Lake counties. If you are in Chicago, this is your gas utility, not Nicor.

programs.name: MidAmerican Energy Efficiency Programs
programs.detail: Electric and gas efficiency rebates for the Illinois communities MidAmerican serves, mainly the Quad Cities area including Rock Island and Moline. Neither ComEd nor Ameren serves these customers.

programs.name: Virtual Power Plant Programs (CRGA)
programs.detail: New under CRGA. Pays households and businesses for smart thermostats, solar, small batteries and EVs dispatched at peak. Utilities filed program details June 1, 2026.

programs.name: Multifamily Retrofit & Preservation Financing
programs.statusNote: IHDA financing is offered through rounds and rolling programs. Confirm the current round with IHDA.
programs.detail: Layered financing for affordable multifamily including energy retrofits and new all-electric construction.

programs.name: Electric Vehicle Rebate Program
programs.statusNote: FY27 cycle open August 1 to December 31, 2026. $14M appropriated; rebates paid as funds allow. Apply within 180 days of purchase.
programs.detail: $2,000 per eligible new or used EV, plus $2,000 more for low-income applicants. Vehicle price under $80,000. Application cycle OPEN August 1 – December 31, 2026. Apply within 180 days of purchase.

programs.name: EV Charging & Transportation Infrastructure
programs.statusNote: Illinois resumed NEVI awards after the 2025 federal freeze was lifted by court order. Confirm the next round with IDOT.
programs.detail: NEVI corridor charging and related transportation infrastructure grants.

programs.name: Section 48E Clean Electricity Investment Credit
programs.detail: 30% base credit. The July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has passed. Projects that started by then have until Dec 31, 2030. Everything starting now must be PLACED IN SERVICE by Dec 31, 2027. Foreign entity sourcing rules apply.

programs.name: Elective Pay (Direct Pay)
programs.statusNote: Still available to tax-exempt owners. Solar and wind starting construction after July 4, 2026 must be placed in service by December 31, 2027. Geothermal and storage run into the 2030s.
programs.detail: Lets nonprofits, churches, municipalities and other tax-exempt owners receive 48E as a cash payment. This is the single most under-used tool in the CBO and municipal stack.

programs.name: 48E for Standalone Storage
programs.detail: Battery storage not co-located with solar is NOT subject to the accelerated solar and wind deadlines. Its longer runway is why storage is the strongest 2027–2030 play.

programs.name: Section 25D Residential Credit
programs.statusNote: Terminated for expenditures after December 31, 2025.
programs.detail: Ended December 31, 2025 with no step-down. Any client still budgeting a 30% homeowner credit has a hole in their pro forma.

programs.name: Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
programs.statusNote: USDA rescinded the FY2025-2027 REAP funding notice on April 15, 2026. A new REAP rule takes effect October 16, 2026; a new funding notice with application windows has not been published. Under the new rule, ground-mount solar or wind on cropland is ineligible and projects must be completed before applying. Do not budget REAP until the new notice is out.
programs.detail: Grants and loan guarantees for rural small businesses and agricultural producers doing efficiency or renewables.

programs.name: DCEO Grant Opportunities — search all programs
programs.detail: Every open DCEO NOFO, not just energy. Grocery initiative, community development, infrastructure, small business — these often cover the capital and construction lines that energy programs will not.

programs.name: Office of Employment & Training — WIOA & regional workforce
programs.detail: Regional Workforce Managers, WIOA-funded training dollars, Apprenticeship Illinois and Job Training Economic Development. This is how a client staffs the project once it is funded.

programs.name: Illinois workNet — local workforce board finder
programs.detail: Find the Local Workforce Innovation Area and American Job Center that serves the client's county. First call for hiring, training dollars and on-the-job training contracts.

programs.name: Office of Entrepreneurship, Innovation & Technology — small business assistance
programs.detail: Small Business Development Centers, Business Information Center, procurement and certification help. The office that gets a contractor bid-ready and a small business bankable.

programs.name: Advantage Illinois — low-interest loan programs
programs.detail: Participation loans and credit enhancement for Illinois small businesses. Pairs with IFA SSBCI on the debt line of a capital stack.

programs.name: Illinois Works — bid credit & contractor resources
programs.detail: Bid credit program and apprenticeship resources for contractors on public works. Relevant to any project carrying prevailing wage or PLA requirements.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency & Conservation Block Grant (EECBG)
programs.statusNote: Final IEPA EECBG round awarded August 2025. No new funding announced. Do not budget it.
programs.detail: DOE/IIJA money for municipal and county strategic energy plans, energy audits and publicly owned building upgrades. Awards ran $50K–$250K. Final round was awarded August 2025 — watch for reauthorization before you budget it. Applicant must be a unit of local government. Schools, school districts and community college districts are not eligible — partner with your municipality, which must be the applicant.

programs.name: Office of Energy — codes training, assessments & trust funds
programs.statusNote: IEPA Office of Energy page lists the Efficient & Resilient Public Buildings Grant ($50K-$200K, local governments, DOE State Energy Program funds) but shows it as both open and closed. Confirm with IEPA before referring.
programs.detail: Energy Code training and technical support, wastewater treatment plant energy assessments, and the Energy Efficiency Trust Fund for low-income and government facilities.

programs.name: Electric School Bus & fleet programs
programs.statusNote: US EPA Clean School Bus is being revamped; no open round as of October 2026 and EPA says new funding details come "later in 2026." IEPA VW school bus rounds are awarded. For fleet trucks see Driving a Cleaner Illinois VW Round 9.
programs.detail: Replacement funding for diesel school buses and public fleet vehicles, prioritizing environmental justice areas.

programs.name: GRID — grid resilience for municipal utilities & co-ops
programs.statusNote: No open NOFO listed as of Oct 27, 2026. Awards active from 2025–2026. IFA may open competitive rolling windows quarterly, subject to funds. Pre-application required. Cost match: 115% of federal funds (large utilities) or one-third plus 15% (small utilities). Eligibility is limited to utility entities in the federal definition; Illinois has requested non-profits and local governments be added, not yet confirmed. Source: Illinois OMB CSFA 560-00-3393.
programs.match: Large utilities: 115% of federal funds. Small utilities: one-third plus 15% of federal funds.
programs.detail: DOE 40101(d) grid resilience grants administered by the Illinois Finance Authority. $150K to $8M. Projects must benefit a state-designated Equity Investment Eligible Community.

programs.name: Small Utility Clean Energy Planning Grant
programs.statusNote: Fourth Round application window listed as 09/01/2026–11/13/2026. Live status on the state grant portal not confirmed. Only municipal and cooperative electric utilities may apply. No match. Source: Illinois OMB CSFA 560-03-3643.
programs.detail: CPRG-funded planning money for municipal and cooperative electric utilities: technical assessments, procurement strategy and PPA readiness. Rolling application plus competitive rounds. Up to $200K per award.

programs.name: Stretch Energy Code adoption support
programs.statusNote: Fourth Round application window listed as 06/15/2026–12/31/2026. Live status on the state grant portal not confirmed. Only Illinois units of local government may apply. No match. Source: Illinois OMB CSFA 560-03-3635.
programs.detail: CPRG-funded planning money to help municipalities adopt, implement and enforce the Illinois Stretch Energy Code — staff time, training and legal review.

program.label: Climate Bank — Stretch Code Adoption Support

programs.name: NEVI, Carbon Reduction, CMAQ & Freight-Port Infrastructure
programs.detail: Four federal formula and competitive programs a village or county can use for corridor charging, fleet depots, congestion and air quality projects, and freight infrastructure.

programs.name: Net metering & distributed generation rules
programs.detail: Retail-rate net metering for systems up to 2 MW, plus the DG installer certification your contractor must hold. Sets what the solar actually earns on the bill.

programs.name: Clean Building Navigator & Concierge (CPRG)
programs.detail: Outreach, intake, contractor coordination and project navigation for residents and small businesses pursuing electrification and efficiency upgrades.

programs.name: Green Resilient Retrofit & Energy Efficiency Program
programs.statusNote: If this relies on HUD GRRP: HUD restructured GRRP effective March 1, 2026 (awards converted to loans, solar and EV chargers no longer fundable). Confirm with IHDA what remains available.
programs.detail: Retrofit and resilience financing for affordable multifamily housing — relevant when a municipality or CBO controls housing stock.

programs.name: Industrial Assessment Center — UIC
programs.detail: DOE-funded program pairing trained staff and students to conduct free energy and pollution assessments at mid-size industrial facilities. UIC is Illinois' center, one of 28 nationally.

programs.name: Private Activity Bonds
programs.detail: Tax-exempt financing for 501(c)(3) organizations and other conduit borrowers to finance or refinance capital expenditures, including clean energy assets. Typical project size $2M+.

programs.name: Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (GGRF)
programs.statusNote: Two tracks, both unresolved. NCIF/CCIA: en banc D.C. Circuit upheld the injunction August 4, 2026; the government is seeking Supreme Court review. Solar for All: termination vacated by federal courts in Rhode Island (Sept. 18, 2026) and D.C. (late Sept. 2026), but funds were not flowing as of October 7 and EPA is weighing appeal. Do not count on this in a capital stack.
programs.detail: Federal program funding clean energy and climate projects in low-income and disadvantaged communities. Solar for All Expansion and National Clean Investment Fund instruments are in litigation with funding paused — confirm current status before counting on this.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency Trust Fund Grant Program
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed (first-come, first-served through June 30, 2026). $50K-$1M with match. Watch for the next IEPA NOFO.
programs.detail: Funds residential energy efficiency projects for public housing authorities, local governments, or nonprofit organizations.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency Assessment Program
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed (through March 31, 2026). $5K-$60K, first-come, first-served. Watch for the next IEPA NOFO.
programs.detail: Grant funding for public housing authorities, local governments, or nonprofit organizations to assess energy efficiency opportunities before committing to a project.

programs.name: Energy Benchmarking & Efficiency at Community Colleges
programs.statusNote: Delivered through IGEN to member colleges, not by open application. No current application window posted. Confirm with IGEN.
programs.detail: Technical assistance and implementation funding to benchmark energy use and complete efficiency upgrades at Illinois community colleges. Delivered through the Illinois Green Economy Network (IGEN), not by direct application to IEPA. Prior awards ran about $106,000 per college, with priority to financially constrained institutions.

programs.name: REV Illinois Act
programs.detail: Reimagining Energy and Vehicles in Illinois Act — a highly competitive incentive program for manufacturers of EVs, EV components, and renewable energy equipment locating or expanding in Illinois.

programs.name: Charging & Fueling Infrastructure Grant
programs.detail: Federal discretionary grant for publicly accessible EV charging and alternative fueling infrastructure, with a rural and community set-aside.

programs.name: Driving a Cleaner Illinois
programs.statusNote: VW Round 9 (all-electric Class 4-8 local freight trucks, up to $18M) open until funds run out. CEJA EV Charging Round 3 closed. No open DERA NOFO. Checked October 8, 2026.
programs.detail: Funded by the Volkswagen settlement and federal DERA dollars. Covers charging station infrastructure and other mobile-source electrification projects, including publicly accessible charging.

programs.name: Returning Resident Clean Jobs Training Program
programs.detail: CEJA program delivering clean jobs training inside Illinois Department of Corrections facilities to individuals within 36 months of release, and post-release support into employment.

programs.name: Become an Equity Eligible Contractor (EEC)
programs.detail: Certification path for Approved Vendors, Designees and Subcontractors majority-owned by an Equity Eligible Persons. Review the eligibility criteria and ways to participate in Illinois Shines as an EEC on the Become an Equity Eligible Contractor (EEC) page on the Illinois Shines website.

programs.name: Energy Equity Portal
programs.detail: The IPA's hub for the clean energy workforce. Register as a clean energy company, post jobs, and connect with job seekers. Also hosts the Small & Emerging Business Hub.

programs.name: Small and Emerging Businesses in Illinois Solar for All and Illinois Shines
programs.detail: To receive the Small and Emerging Business (SEB) designation in both Illinois Shines and Illinois Solar for All Approved Vendors must submit an application and supporting documentation. Benefits include a lower batch threshold for project submittal in Illinois Shines and plus project selection preference and a collateral deduction on REC payments in ILSFA. For more information and to apply click the link below

program.label: Illinois Shines — Become an AV or Designee (SEB)

programs.name: SBA 504 Loans
programs.detail: Long-term, fixed-rate financing for major fixed assets — real estate, equipment — that promote business growth. Usable for clean energy retrofits bundled into a larger capital project.

programs.name: Charitable Trust Grant
programs.detail: General economic development funding for nonprofits. Not clean-energy specific, but usable for a CBO's broader capital campaign.

programs.name: Zero-Emission Vehicle Loan Program
programs.statusNote: Listed as a current program in IFA's October 2026 review. Confirm the application window with IFA.
programs.detail: Climate Bank debt product for converting heavy-duty municipal, business or nonprofit vehicle fleets to electric.

programs.name: ILSFA Bright Neighborhoods Initiative
programs.statusNote: Initiative closed.
programs.detail: An Illinois Solar for All pilot, not Illinois Shines. Tested a consolidated model where the Program Administrator recruited participants directly and matched them to one pre-selected Approved Vendor. Ran in program years 2023-24 and 2024-25 in West Garfield Park and the West Side of Chicago, Waukegan, and the Carbondale-Marion area. Applications are closed; this link is the findings report. Watch for elements of it folding into the main ILSFA program.

programs.name: Solar Training Pipeline Program
programs.detail: Established under the Future Energy Jobs Act (FEJA), now continued through DCEO. Builds a pool of trained solar installers, with priority for foster care alumni and returning citizens. Feeds into Illinois Solar for All projects.

programs.name: Craft Apprenticeship Program
programs.detail: FEJA-established program administered with IBEW to place solar and electrical trades training inside existing union apprenticeship programs statewide.

programs.name: Multicultural Jobs Program
programs.statusNote: Listed as a rolling DCEO opportunity (Future Energy Jobs Act Multi-Cultural) as of October 8, 2026.
programs.detail: FEJA-established program funding diversity-focused community organizations to deliver clean energy job training, sales and business-expansion support.

programs.name: Juntos Crecemos Grant Program
programs.detail: $10,000 grants for woman-owned food and beverage small businesses nationwide. Not clean-energy specific — general small business capital.

programs.name: Pillars of Giving
programs.detail: Nicor's charitable program supporting education, workforce and technical/vocational training aligned with its service territory.

programs.name: Community Empowerment Program
programs.detail: Youth-focused community grants. Not clean-energy specific — relevant if a CBO's clean energy work is bundled with a youth or community facility.

programs.name: Fall Awards
programs.detail: Grants for nonprofits and small businesses across education, workforce development, housing and economic development.

programs.name: Hometown Grants
programs.detail: Capital grants for small-town community development projects nationwide, open to local government and nonprofit applicants.

programs.name: Mission Sustainability Initiative Grants
programs.detail: Capacity-building and strategic planning grants for Illinois nonprofits — useful for a CBO building the organizational capacity to run a clean energy program.

programs.name: Spark Good Local Grants
programs.detail: Local cash grants from nearby Walmart stores and distribution centers for community, youth and education projects.

programs.name: Business & Industry Loan Guarantees
programs.detail: USDA guarantees a commercial lender's loan to a rural business: 85% on requests under $5M, 80% at $5M and up (FY2026). Terms up to 40 years. Covers buildings, land, equipment, machinery, inventory and some refinancing. Rural means outside cities over 50,000. Applied through your lender.

programs.name: Rural Business Development Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 window closed June 30, 2026. Next cycle expected spring 2027.
programs.detail: Grants to public bodies and nonprofits that help small rural businesses: technical assistance, training, feasibility, revolving loan capital. No cost share. Smaller requests get priority. For-profits cannot apply directly.

programs.name: Value-Added Producer Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 window closed April 22, 2026. Next window expected early 2027.
programs.match: 1:1 match (at least 50% of total project cost)
programs.detail: Up to $50K for planning (feasibility, business plans) or $200K for working capital to process and market a value-added agricultural product. Match must be spent before each reimbursement.

programs.name: Community Facilities Direct Loan & Grant
programs.detail: Loans and grants for essential community facilities in rural places of 20,000 or fewer: public buildings, schools, health care, public safety, utility services. Grants cover 15% to 75% of cost depending on population and income. Applications year-round.

programs.name: Rural Energy Savings Program
programs.statusNote: Open first-come, first-served until funds run out.
programs.detail: 0% loans for up to 20 years to electric co-ops and rural utilities, which relend to their members at up to 5% for efficiency, renewables and storage. Consumers do not apply to USDA; ask your co-op if it participates.

programs.name: Biorefinery, Renewable Chemical & Biobased Product Manufacturing Assistance (9003)
programs.statusNote: Accepted year-round with two decision cycles. Next: letter of intent by March 1, Phase 1 by April 1, 2027. Updated rule published July 9, 2026.
programs.detail: Loan guarantees up to $250M for building or retrofitting facilities that make advanced biofuels, renewable chemicals or biobased products with new technology.

programs.name: Advanced Biofuel Payment Program
programs.statusNote: Enrollment open October 1-31, 2026.
programs.detail: Production payments to producers of advanced biofuel made from renewable biomass other than corn kernel starch. Blenders do not qualify.

programs.name: Wood Innovations Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed April 22, 2026.
programs.detail: Expands markets for wood products and wood energy, including mass timber and wood energy feasibility.

programs.name: Community Wood Grants
programs.statusNote: FY26 round closed April 22, 2026.
programs.match: Federal share capped at 35% of capital cost (50% in special cases)
programs.detail: Capital grants for thermally led community wood energy systems and innovative wood product facilities.

programs.name: EDA Public Works & Economic Adjustment Assistance
programs.statusNote: Rolling, no deadline, until a new notice is issued or funds run out.
programs.detail: Infrastructure and economic recovery grants for distressed areas: industrial sites, rail spurs, utilities, workforce facilities. Applicant is a public body, nonprofit or college, not a private business.

programs.name: DRA States' Economic Development Assistance Program
programs.statusNote: 2026 round closed July 31, 2026. Annual.
programs.detail: Infrastructure, workforce and business development grants in the 16 Illinois DRA counties: Alexander, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Jackson, Johnson, Massac, Perry, Pope, Pulaski, Randolph, Saline, Union, White, Williamson.

programs.name: Brownfields Assessment, Cleanup & RLF Grants
programs.statusNote: FY27 solicitations expected fall 2026, due about 60 days after release. No multipurpose grants in FY27.
programs.detail: Assessment up to $500K (coalitions up to $1M), cleanup up to $500K, revolving loan funds up to $1M. Clears contaminated sites for redevelopment, including clean energy siting.

programs.name: EDGE Tax Credit
programs.detail: Income or withholding tax credits for a business that adds jobs in Illinois when the project would not happen here otherwise. 50% of new-hire withholding, 25% for retained jobs, more in underserved areas. Small firms (100 or fewer) need the lesser of 5% growth or 50 jobs.

programs.name: Enterprise Zones
programs.detail: Inside a designated zone: 6.25% state sales tax exemption on building materials, 0.5% investment tax credit, local property tax abatement. Larger projects can get machinery and utility tax exemptions. Ask the local zone administrator.

programs.name: High Impact Business designation
programs.detail: Enterprise-zone-style tax exemptions for very large investments outside a zone, including qualifying wind, solar and storage facilities. Thresholds are high; this is for utility-scale and major manufacturing projects.

programs.name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
programs.statusNote: Economic Development and Community Revitalization are rolling. Public Infrastructure and Housing Rehab are annual competitive rounds.
programs.detail: HUD money for non-entitlement (mostly rural) Illinois communities: public infrastructure ($25M in 2026), housing rehab, community revitalization and economic development. Applicant is the local government.

programs.name: IDOA food and farm infrastructure grants
programs.statusNote: No energy-specific IDOA grant found October 8, 2026. Check each program page for the current round.
programs.detail: Resilient Food Systems Infrastructure, Local Food Infrastructure and Specialty Crop Block Grants fund processing, aggregation and value-added equipment for small farms and food businesses.

programs.name: OSLAD park grants
programs.statusNote: FY27 round closed August 31, 2026. Annual.
programs.detail: Park acquisition (up to $1.125M) and development (up to $600K) for local governments. Relevant when a park building or site upgrade includes efficiency or solar. School districts are not eligible.

programs.name: Illinois brownfields: cleanup loans and free site assessments
programs.statusNote: No posted deadline. Confirm loan funds are available with IEPA.
programs.detail: Brownfields Cleanup Revolving Loan Fund: low or no interest loans for municipally owned sites with an approved remedial plan. Targeted Brownfield Assessments: free soil and groundwater testing for communities.

programs.name: State Revolving Fund (water & wastewater loans)
programs.statusNote: Projects are funded from the annual Intended Use Plan list. Get on the project priority list first.
programs.detail: Low-interest loans for drinking water and wastewater systems, including energy efficiency at treatment plants. Applicant is the local government or utility.

programs.name: First-Time Farmer Bond
programs.statusNote: Lender-driven. Confirm with IFA or your lender.
programs.detail: Lower-rate loan through your own lender for a first-time farmer buying land, farm buildings or new equipment. Net worth up to $500K. Individuals only.

programs.name: Heavy-Duty Charging Vehicle Loan Program

programs.name: Chicago Bungalow Association Energy Savers Program
programs.detail: Program provides weatherization services such as attic insulation, first floor exterior facing wall insulation, furnace or boiler cleaning and tune-ups, high efficiency ventilation fan installation for the bathroom, and weather stripping around windows and doors.

programs.name: Energy Conservation Code Training
programs.detail: Program provides training to increase awareness of the Illinois Energy Conservation Code and to improve the energy efficiency of new constrction and renovation in Illinois through workshops, webinars, online training, resources, and technical support. Training program serves community code official, construction professionals and trade and design professionals such as architects and engineers in Illinois.

programs.name: Energy Conservation Subsidy Exclusion
programs.detail: Energy conservation provided to customers by public utilities are non-taxable. If a taxpayer claims federal tax credits or deductions for the energy conservation property, the investment basis for the purpose of claiming the deduction or tax credit must be reduced by the value of the energy conservation subsidy (i.e., a taxpayer may not claim a tax credit for an expense that the taxpayer ultimately did not pay). Energy subsidies provided to customers by public utilities are non-taxable.

programs.name: Retro-Commissioning (RCx) Program
programs.detail: Retro-commissioning (RCx) ensures that equipment and systems function as intended and operate at optimal efficiency. RCx helps buildings identify what needs to be repaired, tuned, or better maintained to meet needs and reduce energy costs. Energy efficiency services for facilities include energy assessments, COVID-19 readieness building assessments, long-term energy planning, retro-comissioning, new construction design assistance, wastewater treatment plant energy assessments, and energy code assistance.

programs.name: ComEd Commercial New Construction Efficiency Program
programs.detail: Facilities are eligible to receive incentives for new construction, addition/expansion or major renovation of an existing space designed to exceed energy code requirements. This program offers two pathways: the Best practices pathway - a prescriptive approach to new construction projects - and Performance pathway - a custome approach that targets projects in their early design phase to maximize performance improvement opportunities.

programs.name: FHA Energy Efficient Mortgage
programs.detail: Loans can finance the cost of making energy-efficient improvements with heating and cooling systems, such as weatherizing and insulating older homes. FHA insures a borrower's mortgage used to purchase or refinance a principal residence, and the cost of energy efficient imporvements to be made on the home.

programs.name: Peoples Gas / North Shore Gas Custom and New Construction Rebate
programs.detail: Custom rebates are available for energy efficient materials used in the new construction of a building.

programs.name: USDA Single Family Housing Guaranteed Loan Program
programs.detail: Program assists approved lenders in providing low-and moderate-income households the opportunity of homeownership in eligible rural areas. Eligible appliants may purchase, build, rehabilitate, improve, or relocate a dwelling in an eligible rural area with 100% financing.

programs.name: VA Energy Efficient Mortgage
programs.detail: Mortgage is available to qualified military personnel, reservists, and veterans for energy improvements when purchasing an existing home.

programs.name: Fannie Mae HomeStyle Energy Mortgage
programs.detail: Borrowers can make upgrades to reduce utility costs and improve the comfort and safety of their homes by financing energy improvements directly in a purchase or refinance mortgage. Upgrades may also include solar, geothermal, or wind power. In addition, borrowers may use HomeStyle Energy to pay off existing energy debt, including but not limited to PACE loans.

programs.name: Freddie Mac GreenCHOICE Mortgage
programs.detail: Borrowers to finance energy efficient improvements with any mortgage product, property type and financing terms up to 30 years to provide affordable financing opportunities and greater purchasing power despite higher debt-to-income and housing expense-to-income rations for manually underwritten.

programs.name: Energy Savings Performance Contracting Campaign
programs.detail: Campaign engages public sector building owners works with partners to increase awareness of benefits of using performance contracting to increase efficiency, modernize public buildings, reduce utility expenses, and meet lead-by-example goals; share and leverage practical resoruces to build ESPC knowledge and expand ESPEC accessibility across the MUSH market; amplify and implement best practice approaches for ESPC projects and programs; demonstrate impact wiht measured and verified savings.

programs.name: Small Business Illinois On-Bill Energy Efficiency Loan Program
programs.detail: ComEd and Nicor Gas customers are eligible to receive loans up to $150,000 for energy efficiency projects in their buildings. The loan is repaid through an additional charge on the customer's utility bill. Loans can be paid over 1-10 years with a fixed interest rate. There is no penalty for early payment.

programs.name: ComEd Small Business and Facilities Efficiency Program
programs.detail: ComEd customers that operate smaller businesses and facilities (peak demand under 400 kW) are eligible for incentives on energy-saving projects in their buildings. Building owners can submit an interest form and get matched with a ComEd-approved Service Provider that will complete an energy assessment, compile a list of recommendations, and coordinate project delivery. The Service Provider can also apply ComEd incentives to bring project costs down. The program applies to existing buildings looking to pursue energy efficiency upgrades.

programs.name: ComEd Facility Assessments
programs.detail: When scheduled, an approved energy engineer will either conduct an in-person or virtual Facility Assessment. There, they will spend approximately two hours with you assessing your facility to identify energy-efficiency opportunities. Within three to four weeks, you will receive a report detailing energy efficiency projects that you can start working on immediately. Each recommendation will include estimated energy savings, cost savings, project cost, potential incentives and simple payback.

programs.name: ComEd Retro-Commissioning
programs.detail: An authorized Energy Efficiency Service Provider will perform a fully-funded study of your facility’s energy management systems to identify low-cost operational improvements. You’ll save an average of 5-15% on annual energy costs and may also qualify for incentives or additional savings through your natural gas utility’s partnership with ComEd.

programs.name: ComEd High Performance Design Incentive
programs.detail: Program provides free consultations with experienced technical experts and one-time financial incentives for new construction or major renovations designed to exceed energy code requirements. Major renovations are eligible if including significant beyond-code upgrades to at least two major building systems. Additional funds are available for lead design firms that actively engage with the program. ComEd provides recommendations, assistance, and ginancial incetives for energy-saving improvements to all major building systems - envelope, HVAC equipment, lighting, commericial refridgeration, and more.

programs.name: Resurrection Project Home Improvement Loan
programs.detail: Program allows homeowners to borrow up to $30,000 at a 4.99% fixed interest rate for home repairs, home improvements, and energy efficiency-related upgrades in the following Chicago neighborhoods: Archer Heights, Ashburn, Auburn Gresham, Brighton Park, Chicago Lawn, Englewood, Lower West Side, Gage Park, McKinley Park, New City, North Lawndale, South Lawndale, West Englewood, West Elston, West Lawn.

programs.name: Retrofit Chicago Multi-Family Residential Partnership
programs.detail: Provides free energy assessments and assistance with energy efficiency projects. Retrofits for most building types can include weatherization, smart thermostats, lighting, appliance replacements, and HVAC upgrades.

programs.name: ComEd Time-of-Day Pricing
programs.detail: ComEd offers a "dynamic" rate, where the day is divided into three parts with different rates: - Off-Peak (10pm - 6am): 2.447 cents per kWh - Peak (6am - 2pm & 7pm - 10pm): 3.970 cents per kWh - Super Peak (2pm - 7pm): 6.117 cents per kWh Participants can lower their electric bills by putting off heavy electricity usage until the period when the rate is lower.

programs.name: Ameren and ComEd Distributed Generation Rebates
programs.detail: Customers will earn a rebate of $300 per kW of solar and $300 per kWh of energy storage. programs.name: ComEd Peak Time Savings Program
programs.detail: Customers enrolled in this free program receive alerts 3-5 times during the summer to voluntarily lower their electric usage for a few hours, in exchange for bill credits ($1 per kilowatt-hour saved).

programs.name: ComEd Central AC Cycling Program
programs.detail: Customers enrolled in this free program volunteer to have their AC compressors cycled off for 15-minute periods during peak usage in the summer, in exchange for bill credits ($10 per month, $40 total).

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Peak Time Savings Program
programs.detail: Customers earn bill credits by reducing electricity unsafe during peak demand periods, typically on hot afternoons in the summer.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Rebates

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Energy Consultation

programs.name: ComEd Energy Efficient Appliance Discounts and Rebates

programs.name: ComEd Free Energy-Saving Products at Food Pantries
programs.detail: Free LED bulbs, night lights and weatherstripping are available at food pantries in the ComEd service territory. Eligibility for free energy-saving products follows the eligibility criteria for each participating food pantry.

programs.name: ComEd Free Energy Saving Kits
programs.detail: Customers who meet income qualifications may be eligible to receive a free energy savings kit containing energy-saving products such as energy-efficient LED bulbs, high-efficiency faucet aerators, LED night lights, weatherstripping, high-efficiency showerhead, door sweep, window insulation kit, and rope caulk. programs.name: SolarAPP+ Adoption Support
programs.detail: The program will provide grants to permitting units of government that may be used for costs associate with adopting and implementing SolarAPP+, as well as costs associated with updating residential electrical and other codes, if needed to meet SolarAPP+ requirements. programs.name: Residential Solar Outreach Grants

Eligibility: Priority given to applications addressing residents of census tracts identified by the Illinois Solar for All program's Income-Eligible Census Map, as well as geographically distributed residents experiencing low incomes.

programs.name: 40101(d) Grid Resilience
programs.detail: Program will distribute $8 million annually for five years to enhance gird resilience through microgrids, weatherization, automation, and emission-reducing grid upgrades. Expected amounts of individual awards will be between $150,000 to $8,000,000 per project. Eligibility: Secretary of Energy can approve the following additional eligible recipients: non-profit organizations, units of local government, critical facilities, Illinois Municipal Utilities Association (IMUA), Association of Illinois Electric Cooperatives (AIEC).

programs.name: Power Moves Solar Co-Op Program

programs.name: Power Moves Residential Energy Efficiency Rebates
programs.detail: Program offers rebates for energy-efficient upgrades, including dual fuel heat pumps, air source heat pumps (including cold climate models), heat pump water heaters, geothermal heat pumps, and Wi-Fi thermostats.

programs.name: North Shore Gas Home Energy Jumpstart Program
programs.detail: Program provides a free assessment that include free and discounted products for the home. Free installation of these products are available.

programs.name: Nicor Gas Commercial Energy Efficiency Rebates
programs.detail: Commercial customers who install qualifying high-efficiency equipment through a professional contractor between January 1 and December 31, 2025 can receive a rebate. Eligible efficiency technologies include clothes washers, equipment insulation, water heaters, furnaces, boilers, heat recovery, steam-system upgrades, programmable thermostats, energy management systems/building controls, duct/air sealing, processing and manufacturing equipment, agricultural equipment, food service equipment, tankless water heater, attic insulation, and electric clothes dryer.

programs.name: City Water, Light & Power Efficiency Rebates (Springfield)
programs.detail: Program offers rebates for increase energy efficiency of participating homes. Energy efficient air-to-air and geothermal are eligible for rebates which vary according to the technology type, cooling capacity, cooling efficiency, and category.

programs.name: IMUA Training
programs.detail: Program provides on-site programs and services designed to serve the needs of its members, a well as provide assistance in satisfying compliance with various regulatory directives and requirements. Examples of safety topics and programs offered include: arc-blase/arc-flash protection and prevention, confined space enetry and resuce, electrical safety, emergency planning and disaster preparedness, flagger training and certification, hazardous communications, lockout/tagout (LO/TO), pole-top and bucket rescue, trenching and shoring, respiratory protection, and First Aid/CPR/AED.

programs.name: IMEA Demand Response Program
programs.detail: Customers can receive a billing credit incentive from the IMEA for voluntarily agreeing to keep their electric use at or b elow a specified amount when called upon during a Demand Response Event.

programs.name: Distributed Generation Energy Project Financing
programs.detail: Program can provide loans and loan guarantees to energy project developers for distributed energy projects including renewables that provide wholesale or retails electricity to existing Electric Program borrowers or to rural communities served by other utilites.

programs.name: Electric Infrastructure Loan and Loan Guarantee Program
programs.detail: Program makes insured loans and loan guarantees to nonprofit and cooperative associations, public bodies, and other utilities. Insured loans primarily finance the construction of electric distribution, transmission, and generation facilities, including system improvements and replacement required to furnish and improve electric service in rural areas, as well as demand side management, energy conservation programs, and on-grid and off-grid renewable energy systems.

programs.name: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Loan Program
programs.detail: Program provides loans to finance energy efficiency and conservation projects for commercial, industrial, and residential consumers. Eligible utilities can borrow money tied to Treasury rates of interset and re-lend the money to develop new and diverse energy service products within their service territories.

programs.name: Energy Resource Conservation
programs.detail: Program enables borrowers to make funds available to customers for energy conservation and renewable energy projects by deferring payment of principal and interest.

programs.name: High Energy Costs Grants
programs.detail: Program assists energy providers and other eligible entities in lowering energy costs for families and individuals in communities with extremely high per-household energy costs (275 percent of national average or higher). Eligibility: Eligible communities must demonstrate annual average household energy cost exceeding 275 percent of the national average under benchmarks published in the 2025 High Energy Cost Grant Funding Opportunity Announcement. https://www.rd.usda.gov/about-rd/agencies/rural-utilities-service.

programs.name: Rural Economic Development Loan and Grant Programs
programs.detail: Program provides funding for rural projects through zero-interest loans to local utilities which they, in turn, pass through to local businesses for projects that will create and retail employment in rural areas. Maximum grant amount of $300,000 to establish the Revolving Loan Fund and a maximum loan amount of $1 million.

programs.name: CIC Energy Savers Program
programs.detail: Bundle energy conservation expenses into an overall acquisition/rehab or refinance loan to finance your practical retrofit work: replace a boiler, improve air sealing and insulation, install a high-efficiency water heater, and more. Receive a free comprehensive building assessment and access to utility grant funds through CIC’s Energy Savers program.

programs.name: Chicago Solar Express
programs.detail: Provides reduced fees and permitting and zoning assistance to facilitate rooftop solar installations.

programs.name: ComEd Business and Public Sector EV Program
programs.detail: Rebates are available for business and public sector customers to purchase or lease new, pre-owned, and repowered battery electric vehicles: https://www.comed.com/about-us/clean-energy/electric-vehicle-rebate-program. Eligibility: Customers who reside in or serve a low-income of Equity Investmet Eligible community are eligible for a large rebate.

programs.name: ComEd Business and Public Sector Make-Ready Rebate Program
programs.detail: Rebates are available for business and public sector customers for completed make-ready projects that include the infrastructure necessary to install electric vehicle (EV) charging stations from the transformer to the EV charging station's stub. Eligibility: Projects installed in low-income or an Equity Investment Eligible Community and/or customers who demosntrate through attestation that over 50% of the driving done by their business fleet vehicles using the make-ready infrastructure applying for a rebate serves one of those communities. https://www.comed.com/about-us/clean-energy/make-ready-rebate-program.

programs.name: ComEd Fleet Electrification Assessment
programs.detail: The ComEd Fleet Electrification Assessment provides an assessment to identify vehicles and charging infrastructure that can support fleet electrification.

programs.name: Qualified Commercial Clean Vehicle Credit (Section 45W)
programs.statusNote: Terminated for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.
programs.detail: Businesses and tax-exempt organizations that buy a qualified commericial clean vehicle may qualify for a clean vehicle tax credit of up to $40,000 under Internal Revenue Code (IRC) 45W. Ended for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.

programs.name: IEPA Charging Incentive Program
programs.detail: IEPA provides funding to public and private organizations and companies to install and maintain publicly-available Level 2 of Level 3 charging stations.

programs.name: Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit (Section 30C)
programs.statusNote: Terminated for property placed in service after June 30, 2026.
programs.detail: Credit for alternative fuel vehicle refueling property, including EV charging stations, of up to 30% of the cost to purchase and install the equipment, available in qualified locations. Ended for property placed in service after June 30, 2026.

programs.name: Federal Airport Zero Emission Vehicle and Infrastructure Incentives
programs.detail: This program allows airport sponsors to use Airport Improvement Program funds to purchase zero emissions vehicles and to construct or modify infrastructure needed to use electric vehicles.

programs.name: CTA Reduced Fare and Free Ride Programs
programs.detail: Certain CTA riders qualify for reduced fares or can ride the CTA for free.

programs.name: RTA Discounted Fare and Ride Free Programs
programs.detail: Ride Free Permit allows seniors age 65 and over or individuals with disabilities under the age of 65 to ride at no cost on CTA, Metra, and Pace bus and rail service. Applicants must be enrolled in the Benefit Access Program administered by the Illinois Department of Aging.

programs.name: Ameren Free Fleet Assessment
programs.detail: This assessment will help customers evaluate their vehicle fleets to understand the business and technical information needed to make a decision about converting their fleets to electric. This program will provide financial, environmental, and technical impacts to help with the decision for converting to an electric fleet.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois ChargeSmart Program (Non-Residential)
programs.detail: This program supports multifamily, education, fleet, transit, corridor, and public charging facilities in adopting EV charging solutions with incentives, tools, and guidance to manage energy usage effectively,.

programs.name: Ameren EV Community Engagement Consultation Program
programs.detail: A free consultation that provides funding, resources, and support to help communities transition to electric vehicles and transportation infrastructure.

programs.name: Ameren Drivers Education Program
programs.detail: This program offers free electrical vehicle resources and rebates for high school driving programs in eligible communities to purchase an EV and charger. EV Curriculum Support is available to all driving education programs.

programs.name: Ameren ChargeSmart Program (Residential)
programs.detail: Customers are encouraged to charge their electric vehicles during off-peak hours. Customers receive bill credits for charging their Evs during the utility's preferred charging hours (11pm to 7am) and may incur extra charges for charging during no-preferred hours (11am to 7pm).

programs.name: Ameren Level 2 Charger Incentive
programs.detail: Qualified EV drivers can install or upgrade their EV charger at no cost. The incentive includes all electrician costs, any panel upgrades, and the charger itself.

programs.name: Clean Heavy-Duty Vehicles Grant Program
programs.detail: Grants are provided to incentivize and accelerate the replacement of existing internal combustion engine heavy-duty vehicles with zero-emission vehicles. Funding may be used for zero emission vehicle refueling infrastructure, workforce development and training, and project implementation costs.

programs.name: Clean Vehicle Credit (Section 30D)
programs.statusNote: Terminated for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.
programs.detail: Tax credit of up to $7,500 for buying a new EV between 2023 to 2032 that is bought for one's onw use and is used primarily in the U.S. Ended for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.

programs.name: Previously Owned Clean Vehicle Credit (Section 25E)
programs.statusNote: Terminated for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.
programs.detail: Tax credit of up to $4,000 buying a used EV in 2023 or after. Ended for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025.

programs.name: Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program (ITEP)
programs.detail: Program provides $140 million in state and federal funding for walking, biking, and trail projects around Illinois.

programs.name: Safe Routes to School (SRTS) Grant
programs.detail: A bi-annual funding opportunity that funds programming and infrastructure projects that improve conditions for walking and biking wihtinn 2-milies of an elementary, middle, or high school.

programs.name: IMEA EV and Charging Incentive Program
programs.detail: Municipalities can use $250,000 to establish a locally managed EV Charging Station Program so that municipalities can provide incentives to retail customers that install qualified EV charging stations; and/or incentivize up to 100% of the cost of purchasing or leasing for the municipality a level 2 or level 3 EV charging station; and/or incentivize up to 100% of the cost of purchasing or leasing for the municipality an Electric Vehicle; and/or transger funds for the city use int eh IMEA Electric Efficiency Program.

programs.name: Rural and Tribal Assistance Pilot Program
programs.detail: Program provides grants to support legal, technical, and financial advisors to help advance infrastructure projects. Eligible project sponors may receive grant funds to select advisors to assist with predevelopment phase activities, including: feasibility studies, project planning, revenue forecasting and funding and financing options analyses, preliminary engineering and design work, environmental review, economic assessments and cost-benefit analyses, public benefits studies, statutory and regulatory framework analyses, value-for-money (VFM) studies, evaluation of costs to sustain the project, evaluation opoortunities for private financing and project bundling.

programs.name: Higher Blends Infrastructure Incentive Program
programs.detail: $90 million is made available each quarter for activities related to higher blends of fuel ethanol greater than 10 percent ethanol, such as E15 or higher, and biodiesel greater than 5 percent biodiesel, such as B20 or higher, as well as activities related to higher blends of fuel ethanol greater than 10 percent.

programs.name: Strategic EV Component Part Manufacturing
programs.detail: Program supports the expansion of electric vehicle component and vehicle manufacturing in McLean County by funding capital improvements.

programs.name: Infield Conservation for Operationalizing Vital Ecosystem Resilience (I-COVER)
programs.detail: Program offers cost-share/financial incentives through the Partners for Conservation (PFC) Program to producers and landowners who seed cover crops in the late summer and fall.

programs.name: Leaking Underground Storage Tank Fund
programs.detail: Program helps tank owners and operators pay for cleaning up leaks from petroleum underground storage tanks by paying for site investigation, site cleanup, laboratory services, and engineering oversight. A maximum of $1,500,000 is available per occurrence. Eligibility: USTs must have reported a petroleum release and have registered their tanks with the Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal.

programs.name: Cover Crops Premium Discount Program
programs.detail: Program offers applicants a premium discount up to $5 per acre on the following year's crop insurance for every cover crop acre enrolled and verified in the program.

programs.name: Specialty Crop Block Grant
programs.detail: Funds will support projects that expand the availability of fresh, locally-grown produce and strengthen the competitiveness of the state's specialty crop industry.

programs.name: Ag Invest Loan Program
programs.detail: Program provides farmers, agri-business, and agriculture professionals below-market rate loans to start, expand or add value to their farm operations. The loans can be used for the purchase of farm equipment, purchase of land, construction-related expenses, provide operating lines of credit, or other costs related to conventional or sustainable farming.

programs.name: BioPreferred Program
programs.detail: The two major parts of the Program are mandatory purchasing requirements for federal agencies and their contractors and a voluntary labeling initiative for biobased products.

programs.name: Fertilizer Production Expansion Program
programs.detail: Provides grants to help eligible applicants increase or otherwise expand the manufacturing and processing of fertilizer and nutrient alternatives and their availability in the United States. The maximum award amount is $100 million. The minimum award amount is $1 million.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Farm Energy Audit
programs.detail: Program offers a Free Energy Audit for Agricultural Facilities, providing a great step towards a more cost effective operation. In addition to the Free Energy Audit, participants in this program will receive both technical and implementation support so that energy-efficiency opportunities identified during the audit can be implemented successfully to save both energy and money.

programs.name: Resilient Food Systems Infrastructure (RFSI) Program
programs.detail: Program provides funding to expand the capacity and market opportunities for local and regional producers in the middle of the food supply chain (processing and aggregation/distribution).

programs.name: Illinois Local Food Infrastructure Grant
programs.detail: Program is intended to assist Illinois applicants with purchasing, leasing to own, renting, building or installation of infrastructure that will increase market access of Illinois agricultural products to Illinois communities. Funding can support value-added processing, livestock, processing, milling, dairy, refrigerated vehicles, food hubs, community kitchens, and other critical pieces of the local food supply chain.

programs.name: Innovative Agriculture Micro-grants for Chicago (IAM-Chi)
programs.detail: Grants are designed to fund innovating, forward-thinking, and novel projects to advance urban agriculture in Chicago. Grants will support conservation practices which improve soil quality, support or provide cost-share for infrastructure and on-farm equipment, or improve supply chain issues, among other activities. Grants will range in amount, from $1,000 (minimum) to $25,000 (maximum) in funding. Grants are small, one-time allocations awarded to eligible producers for short-term projects.

programs.name: Farmer Veteran Fellowship Fund
programs.detail: Grant program that provides direct assistance to veterans who are in their beginning years of farming or ranching. The Fellowship Fund does not give money directly to the veteran, but rather to third-party vendors for items the veteran has identified will make a crucial difference in the launch of their farm business. Awards range from $1,000 to $5,000, and nearly $4 million has been awarded to more than 930 veterans since 2011.

programs.name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP)
programs.detail: Program encouragers farmers and landowners to enroll in long-term conservation contracts, removing environmentally sensitive land from agricultural production and implementing conservation practices. Participants receive annual rental payments, cost-share assistance for establishing conservation practices, and other financial incentives.

programs.name: Climate-Smart Agriculture and Farm Loan Programs
programs.detail: Program offers financials support to farmers and ranchers seeking to adopt climate-smart practices. The loans cover a wide range of activities, including conservation projects, renewable energy systems, and other climate-smart technologies.

programs.name: Conservation Reserve Program (CRP)
programs.detail: A voluntary program that encourage agricultural producers and landowners to convert highly erodible and other environmentally sensitive acreage to vegetative cover, such as native grasses, trees, and riparian buggers. By enrolling, participants receive annual rental payments and cost-share assistance to establish long-term, resource-conserving vegetative covers.

programs.name: Grassland Conservation Reserve Program
programs.detail: A federally funded voluntary program that contracts with agricultural producers so that environmentally sensitive agricultural land is not farmed, but instead used for conversation. Participants receive rental payments and cost-share assistance. Contract duration is 10 to 15 years.

programs.name: Farmable Wetlands Program (FWP)
programs.detail: Program encourages farmers and landowners to restore farmable wetlands and establish conservation practices to improvements, targeting specific areas of non-floodplain wetlands that are suitable for restoration. Participants receive annual rental payments, cost-share assistance for establishing conservation practices, and other financial incentives for the duration of their contract, typically 10 to 15 years.

programs.name: Graze-Out Program
programs.detail: Program is available to producers who elect to use their acreage planted to wheat, barley, oats, or triticale for grazing by livestock and agree to forgo any other harvesting of the commodity on such acreage during the applicable crop year. Eligible commodities include barley, oats, wheat, and tricale. Payments are made to these producers.

programs.name: Tree Assistance Program (TAP)
programs.detail: Program offers financial support to orchardists and nursery tree growers who experience losses due to natural disasters by covering the cost of replanting or rehabilitating eligible trees, bushes, and vines that produce annual crops and have been damaged or destroyed.

programs.name: Water-Saving Commodities (WSC) Program
programs.detail: Program supports agricultural commodity production while reducing water losses in places experiencing impacts from drought. Grants will help producers, and the organizations delivering water to producers, build long-term drought resilience and expand market opportunities.

programs.name: Youth Loans
programs.detail: Loans are designed support young individuals in pursuing agricultural projects that generate income and promote hands-on learning in farming, ranching, and agricultural business management. Loan amounts are up to $10,000 per eligible applicant.

programs.name: Illinois Conservation Stewardship Program (property tax incentive)
programs.detail: Landowners outside of Cook county who have at least five acres of unimproved land and are willing to commit to developing and implementing a habitat management plan for their property may apply for this program in exchange for reduced valuation of property taxes.

programs.name: Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) Grant Program
programs.detail: A grant program that provides up to 50% funding assistance to eligible, local units of government to acquire land for public outdoor recreation areas.

programs.name: Illinois Natural Areas Stewardship Grant Program
programs.detail: Program provides grants to conservation land trusts to increase stewardship on dedicated Illinois Nature Preserves and registered Land and Water Reserves and increase stewardship capacity within conservation land trusts.

programs.name: Agricultural Conservation Easement Program
programs.detail: Program provides financial assistance for purchasing Agricultural Land Easements that protect the agricultural use and conservation values of eligible lands.

programs.name: Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
programs.detail: Program provides technical and financial assistance to agricultural producers and forest landowners to address natural resource concerns. Producers receive support to develop a conservation plan, and financial assistance is available to implement practices.

programs.name: Conservation Reserve Program Transition Incentives Program
programs.detail: Program offers a special incentive of two years of extra CRP rental payments to owners of land that is returning from CRP back into production whor ent or sell their land to underserved producers who commit to using sustianable grazing practices, resource-conserving cropping systems, or transitioning to organic production.

programs.name: Power Moves Commercial and Industrial Rebate Program
programs.detail: Program helps make upgrades, renovations, and new construction projects more affordable by offering rebates on energy-efficient equipment for lighting and non-lighting retrofits. Program provide rebates for commercial accounts that are building a new facility, adding on to an existing facility, or changing the use of an existing facility or completing a total gut rehab. Rebates per building per year are up to $25,000 prescriptive and $50,000 custom. Includes a new construction track for new facilities and additions.

programs.name: Ameren Illinois Instant Incentives Program
programs.detail: Instant incentives are provided for Ameren Illinois businsesses to purchase energy-efficiecny equipment and receive instant discounts. Contractors can receive discounts from participating distributors and pass those savings on their customers. Incentives are split into two categories, Lighting and Non-Lighting incentives.

programs.name: Clean Energy Career Pathway Program
programs.detail: This program will provide funding directly to eligible recipients to support the planning and implmentation of a Clean Energy Career Pathway. Programs will include coursework, dield experiences, and work-based learning designed to prepare students for entrance into careers focusing on electric vehicles. Awards will range from $250,000 - $750,000.

programs.name: Displaced Energy Worker Dependent Transition Scholarship Program
programs.detail: Program provides assistance to children (including adopted and stepchildren) of eligible displaced energy workers. Tuition and fees at public colleges or community colleges are covered for a period equal to one calendar year, including a summer terms, for undergraduate or graduate study.

programs.name: University Training and Research for Fossil Energy and Carbon Management
programs.detail: Program aims to educate and train the next generation of engineers and scientists; support novel, early-stage research at U.S. colleges and universities; increase research and development opporunities for underrepresented and structurally marginalized communities; ensure that students are being equipped with cutting-edge, translatable skillsets that will allow them to contribute to the U.S. workforce and greater economy over the course of a longstanding and enduring career.

programs.name: Farm Labor Stabilization and Protection Pilot Grant Program
programs.detail: Program provides grants to employers to adopt practices that promote labor retention, enhance worker safety and health, and ensure compliance with labor laws and regulations.

programs.name: Public Water Supply Energy Efficiency Grant Program and Assessments
programs.detail: Program provides funding for energy efficiency upgrades at public water supply facilities, also referred to as drinking water treatment plants. Awards will range from $20,000 to $500,000. Projects must reduce the amount of energy consumed by the water treatment operations and must be identified in an energy efficiency assessment completed within the last 5 years. Program provides no-cost energy use assessments in partnership with the Smart Energy Design Assistance Center (SEDAC).

programs.name: Advanced Energy Project Credit (Section 48C)
programs.detail: Manufacturers and other entities that invest in qualifying advanced energy projects may apply for a credits equal to 30% of qualified investment costs for projects that meet prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements or 6% of projects that don't meet prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements. Eligibility: Qualifying projects: '- Re-equips, expands or establishes an industrial or a manufacturing facility to produce or recycle specified advanced energy property - Installs technology in an industrial or manufacturing facility to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 20% - Re-equips, expands or establishes an industrial facility to process, refine or recycle critical materials.

programs.name: Critical Aspects of Sustainability: Innovative Solutions to Climate Change
programs.detail: Program encourages submisison of proposals to lay the foundation for interdisciplinary research to answer fundamental questions related to novel apporaches and solutions to climate change and reduce GHG emissions and concentrations. Topics may include improved or new apporaches that reduce energy use and energy waste relevant for manufacturing, recycling, and upcycling; strategies for reducing nitrous oxide and methan emissoins; reduction in energy use and increased energy efficiency in manufacturing; new smart technologies for homes, cities, communities, power grids, etc. Also supports projects to host conferences and workshops. Maximum funding request of $100,000.

programs.name: DOE Loan Guarantee Program
programs.detail: Loan guarantees are issued for projects with high technology risks and are intended to encourage early commericial use of new or significantly improved technologies in energy projects, specifically in innovative clean energy, advanced transportation, and Tribal energy projects.

programs.name: Special Assessment for Solar Energy Systems
programs.detail: Illinois offers a special assessment of solar energy systems for property tax purposes. When a claim for alternate valuation is filed, the chief county assessment officer is required to ascertaion two values: the value of the improvements as if equipped with a conventional heating or cooling system and the the value of the improvements as equipped with the solar energy system. Eligible equipment includes both active and passive solar energy systems.

programs.name: IMUA Scholarship Program
programs.detail: Winners of the scholarship receives a $1,000 award from IMUA to be used for college tuition and other college related expenses.
